description: The isWorking input of the status derivation (DESIGN v2.6 §B, v1.4 'Status derivation'): the agent counts as working when the harness itself is working, or when PowerUp is in remote mode and a remote turn is active (hooks bracket the turn: UserPromptSubmit to Stop). A remote turn flag left over in built-in mode is ignored. Every combination of harness state (stopped, starting, ready, working), mode and remote turn flag (16 rows).
function: AppState.derivedIsWorking(harnessState:isRemoteMode:remoteTurnActive:) — input {harnessState, isRemoteMode, remoteTurnActive} in, Bool out
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v1.4 addendum (status derivation in remote mode) and v2.6 addendum §B, plus characterization of the Swift implementation (spec #94, ticket #125); Tests/PowerUpTests/StatusDerivationTests.swift. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/status.rs working_cases runs status::derived_is_working.

cases.name: built-in, harness stopped
cases.reason: No session is running, so nothing is working.

cases.name: built-in, harness starting
cases.reason: Spawning the CLI is not a turn: the light stays at rest until a prompt is actually being worked on.

cases.name: built-in, harness ready
cases.reason: A ready session waiting for a prompt is not working.

cases.name: built-in, harness working
cases.reason: The built-in turn is the ordinary source of the amber light.

cases.name: built-in ignores a stale remote turn, harness stopped
cases.reason: Remote turns only count in remote mode; a flag left behind must never pin the light amber in built-in mode.

cases.name: built-in ignores a stale remote turn, harness starting
cases.reason: Remote turns only count in remote mode, whatever the harness is doing.

cases.name: built-in ignores a stale remote turn, harness ready
cases.reason: Remote turns only count in remote mode, whatever the harness is doing.

cases.name: built-in, harness working, stale remote turn
cases.reason: The built-in turn alone is enough; the stale flag changes nothing.

cases.name: remote, no turn, harness stopped
cases.reason: The normal remote resting state: our own session is stopped and no hooked session is mid-turn.

cases.name: remote, no turn, harness starting
cases.reason: A harness that is only starting is not working, in either mode.

cases.name: remote, no turn, harness ready
cases.reason: A ready harness is not working, in either mode.

cases.name: remote, no turn, harness still working
cases.reason: Characterization: the harness state is trusted in either mode, so a built-in turn still winding down right after the switch to remote keeps the light amber until the harness reports it has stopped (the switch to remote mode stops our own session).

cases.name: remote turn active, harness stopped
cases.reason: Remote mode has no process of ours to watch (the harness is stopped there); the hooks bracket the turn instead.

cases.name: remote turn active, harness starting
cases.reason: The remote turn alone is enough.

cases.name: remote turn active, harness ready
cases.reason: The remote turn alone is enough.
